name: json-server
description: JSON Server - A lightweight mock REST API server with file-based data persistence

security.authentication: none - endpoints are unauthenticated by default
security.session: none - no session management middleware included
security.json_payload_validation: REQUIRED - All POST/PUT payloads MUST be validated against schema.json before persistence. Use JSON Schema validator (ajv recommended) to enforce type and structure constraints.
security.sensitive_data: Test fixtures (fixtures/db.json, fixtures/db.json5) must NOT contain credentials, API keys, passwords, or PII. Use environment variables for sensitive data in development.
security.notes: This is a development/prototyping tool. For production use, implement auth middleware (e.g., JWT, OAuth2), enforce access controls, validate all JSON payloads, and sanitize user input.

author: typicode <typicode@gmail.com>

scripts._security-note: IMPORTANT: All file paths used with lowdb or fs operations MUST be validated to prevent directory traversal (../ attacks). Use path.resolve() and path.normalize() followed by a whitelist/prefix check.

devDependencies._comment: Path validation required for all user-controlled file paths. Example pattern: const safeDbPath = (userPath) => { const resolved = path.resolve(process.cwd(), userPath); if (!resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(process.cwd()))) throw new Error('Path traversal detected'); return resolved; }. Use path.normalize() and verify resolved path stays within allowed base directory before passing to lowdb or fs operations.
